title: Computerised CTG Changes During Mechanical Cervical Ripening With Balloon or Dilapan-S
official: Computerised Cardiotocographic Changes During Mechanical Cervical Ripening With a Double-Balloon Catheter or a Synthetic Osmotic Dilator (MECH-cCTG): a Prospective Observational Cohort Study
summary: Mechanical cervical ripening (balloon catheters and synthetic osmotic dilators) is considered safe for the fetus because it rarely causes uterine tachysystole. However, its effect on fetal heart rate control has never been measured objectively. This study uses computerised cardiotocography (cCTG, Dawes-Redman analysis) to measure fetal heart rate parameters before and after insertion of a double-balloon catheter (CRB) or Dilapan-S in women undergoing induction of labour. Each woman has three 60-minute cCTG recordings: before insertion, immediately after insertion, and at device removal after 12 hours. The main question is whether short-term variation (STV) changes after insertion, and whether changes differ between the two devices.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Singleton pregnancy in cephalic presentation
* Gestational age 34+0 weeks or more, dated by first-trimester crown-rump length
* Clinical indication for induction of labour
* Unfavourable cervix (Bishop score below 6) with planned ripening by double-balloon catheter or Dilapan-S
* Intact membranes
* Written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Labour, regular painful contractions or ruptured membranes at enrolment
* Contraindication to vaginal birth or to mechanical ripening (placenta praevia or low-lying placenta, active genital infection, active vaginal bleeding)
* Major fetal structural or chromosomal anomaly, or fetal arrhythmia
* Maternal drugs that alter fetal heart rate variation in the previous 7 days (corticosteroids, magnesium sulphate, beta-blockers, opioids, benzodiazepines) or methyldopa started within 48 hours
* Any pharmacological ripening agent before or during the study period
* Maternal fever 38 degrees C or higher, or maternal heart rate above 100 bpm at baseline
* Baseline computerised CTG not meeting Dawes-Redman criteria within 60 minutes
